recordedWith: the managed path's recorded table (voni/src/lib/voice/barge-in-recovery.cases.json) plus the spec's M09 case catalogue (double barge-in, expiry, greeting, goodbye, tool-hold)
comment: The cross-engine barge-in table. recoveryRows names every row of the managed table the cascade must pass unchanged; the runner reads those rows from the managed file rather than copying them, so a missing managed row or a changed expected tail fails by name. cases are the lifecycle rows from the spec; each row names its source case and the observables the cascade must produce. A difference from a recorded value is a bug, not a new expected value.
recoveryRows: a filler barge-in resumes the exact unheard tail from the last heard word
a noise with no caller words still resumes the unheard tail
a cut after the last word has nothing left unheard
a tail of three words or fewer is not worth resuming
hearing only the first word keeps the whole line, heard word included
a line that played in full leaves only the overlap word, never a restart

cases.name: double barge-in keeps one acknowledgement per cancel and the latest caller turn wins
cases.source: M09 AC4; spec "Barge-in on Cancel" — Double barge-in

cases.name: a cancel after expiry gets no acknowledgement; playback stops locally
cases.source: spec case "Cancel is sent after expires_at"

cases.name: a greeting barge-in cancels the greeting and the caller wins
cases.source: spec case "A barge-in arrives during the greeting"; M07 AC3

cases.name: a goodbye barge-in cancels the closing line and the caller wins
cases.source: spec case "A barge-in arrives during the goodbye"

cases.name: a tool-hold barge-in cancels the hold and the tool result still lands
cases.source: spec case "A real interruption happens during a tool hold"; M08 AC5
